original_question: For every successor cardinal κ, must the negative relation \((2^κ over κ) ↛ (2^κ over κ)^(1,1)_2\) hold? Equivalently, is there always a 2-coloring of 2^κ × κ with no monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^κ and κ?
target_in_paper: Problem 4.1 in Section 4 ("Polarized partition relations at uncountable cardinals"): whether, for every successor cardinal κ, the negative strong polarized relation \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2 holds. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official target very closely: it uses the same pair (2^κ, κ), the same two-color strong polarized relation, the same negative arrow, and the same coloring reformulation in terms of forbidding a monochromatic rectangle of sizes 2^κ and κ. Definition 1.1 gives exactly this meaning to the polarized-arrow notation. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
missing_details: The paper phrases this as an open ZFC-style question ("Does the negative relation ... hold for every successor cardinal κ?"), not as a consistency or forcing question. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
Because it appears in Section 4, which is devoted to uncountable cardinals, κ is intended as an uncountable successor cardinal. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

To make the statement fully stand-alone, the negative relation should be unpacked explicitly: there exists a coloring c: 2^κ × κ → 2 such that for every A ⊆ 2^κ and B ⊆ κ with |A| = 2^κ and |B| = κ, the restriction c|(A × B) is not constant. This is the negation of Definition 1.1. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
Homogeneous or monochromatic means constant on the entire rectangle A × B, and the subscript 2 means exactly two colors. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))

The nearby motivation should remain visible: immediately before Problem 4.1 the paper recalls a positive consistency result for \binom{2^\mu}{\mu} \to \binom{2^\mu}{\mu}^{1,1}_2 from a supercompact cardinal, so this problem asks for the opposite universal statement at successor κ and should not be shifted to the neighboring \binom{\kappa^+}{\kappa} question. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
refined_question: Does ZFC prove that for every uncountable successor cardinal κ, \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa} \nrightarrow \binom{2^\kappa}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2; equivalently, is there a coloring c: 2^\kappa \times \kappa \to 2 such that for no A \subseteq 2^\kappa and B \subseteq \kappa with |A| = 2^\kappa and |B| = \kappa is c constant on A \times B?
justification: The exact official formulation nearest your draft is Problem 4.1. Its placement in Section 4 shows that the scope is uncountable cardinals, and the discussion immediately before it recalls the known positive consistency result \binom{2^\mu}{\mu} \to \binom{2^\mu}{\mu}^{1,1}_2 for some supercompact μ. Definition 1.1 is the place where the polarized-arrow notation is unpacked into the coloring/monochromatic-rectangle formulation, so making that negation explicit is the right way to turn the paper’s notation into a sharp stand-alone question. This is why the refined version stays exactly at the pair (2^κ, κ), with two colors and full rectangles of sizes 2^κ and κ, and does not drift to the neighboring (κ^+, κ) problem or to a mere consistency variant. ([shelah.logic.at](https://shelah.logic.at/files/95093/1012.pdf))
